memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Visit for newly diagnosed psoriasis and irritable bowel syndrome.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports scaly plaques on elbows and knees for 3 months and intermittent abdominal bloating with loose stools after meals.
EXAMINATION: BP 118/76 mmHg, weight 52 kg, height 1.58 m, BMI 20.8 (normal). Plaques are erythematous with silvery scale, Auspitz sign positive. Abdomen soft, non‑tender, no masses.
IMPRESSION: Plaque psoriasis, mild. IBS‑diarrhoea subtype likely.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start clobetasol 0.05% cream BD to plaques, calcipotriol ointment OD, methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly with folic acid 5 mg OD. For IBS: mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Return if: worsening skin lesions, joint pain, fever >38.5°C, bloody stools, or severe abdominal pain. Influenza vaccine offered today, patient declined.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
clobetasol 0.05% cream – apply BD to affected areas – 4 weeks
calcipotriol ointment – apply OD – 4 weeks
methotrexate 7.5 mg – take once weekly – 12 weeks
folic acid 5 mg – take OD – 12 weeks
mebeverine 135 mg – take BD – 8 weeks
ispaghula husk 5 g – take OD with water – 8 weeks
loperamide 2 mg – take SOS after loose stool – 8 weeks

memories.author: lab
memories.text: LFT: ALT 28 U/L (≤40), AST 24 U/L (≤37), ALP 78 U/L (30‑120), bilirubin 0.6 mg/dL (0.2‑1.2). CBC: Hb 12.8 g/dL (12‑16), WBC 6.2×10⁹/L (4‑10), platelets 210×10⁹/L (150‑400). Creatinine 0.7 mg/dL (0.5‑0.9). Stool routine: ova and cysts nil, pus cells 0‑1/hpf. tTG‑IgA: <2 U/mL (negative <7).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Review of labs and symptom control.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Psoriasis plaques less erythematous, mild itching; IBS symptoms unchanged, occasional bloating.
EXAMINATION: BP 122/78 mmHg, weight 53 kg, BMI 21.2 (normal). Plaques show reduced scale, no new lesions. Abdomen benign.
IMPRESSION: Psoriasis improving on current regimen; LFTs normal. IBS stable.
ARRANGEMENTS: Reduce methotrexate to 5 mg weekly due to mild transaminitis trend, keep folic acid 5 mg OD. Continue topicals and IBS meds. Return if: skin flare, joint swelling, fever >38.5°C, mucus/blood in stool, or worsening abdominal pain. Influenza vaccine offered, patient declined.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
methotrexate 5 mg – take once weekly – 12 weeks
folic acid 5 mg – take OD – 12 weeks
(clobetasol, calcipotriol, mebeverine, ispaghula husk, loperamide unchanged)

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Follow‑up after 3 months.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports clear skin, minimal itching; IBS symptoms well controlled with occasional use of loperamide.
EXAMINATION: BP 119/76 mmHg, weight 54 kg, BMI 21.6 (normal). No active plaques, slight post‑inflammatory hypopigmentation. Abdomen soft, non‑tender.
IMPRESSION: Psoriasis in remission; IBS controlled.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Give influenza vaccine today (0.5 mL IM) – patient accepted. Return if: new plaques, joint pain, fever >38.5°C, blood/mucus in stool, or severe abdominal discomfort.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Influenza vaccine – 0.5 mL IM – given today
(clobetasol 0.05% cream BD, calcipotriol ointment OD, methotrexate 5 mg weekly, folic acid 5 mg OD, mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS)

memories.author: lab
memories.text: LFT: ALT 22 U/L, AST 20 U/L, ALP 75 U/L, bilirubin 0.5 mg/dL. CBC: Hb 13.0 g/dL, WBC 5.8×10⁹/L, platelets 205×10⁹/L. Creatinine 0.68 mg/dL. Stool routine: normal. tTG‑IgA: <2 U/mL (negative).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Review of normal labs and disease status.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Skin remains clear; IBS symptoms occasional, well managed.
EXAMINATION: BP 120/77 mmHg, weight 55 kg, BMI 22.0 (normal). No lesions, no mucosal changes.
IMPRESSION: Psoriasis remission; IBS stable. Labs normal.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase methotrexate back to 7.5 weekly, continue folic acid 5 mg OD. Continue topicals as needed PRN. IBS meds unchanged. Return if: skin plaques reappear, joint swelling, fever >38.5°C, blood/mucus in stool, or worsening abdominal pain. Influenza vaccine status: up‑to‑date (given Oct 2025).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
methotrexate 7.5 mg – take once weekly – 12 weeks
folic acid 5 mg – take OD – 12 weeks
(other meds unchanged)

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve noticed a few red, itchy patches on my scalp and behind my ears over the past week. My bowel habits are fine, just occasional bloating after lunch.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Visit for scalp psoriasis flare.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: New itchy plaques on scalp and retroauricular area for 7 days; IBS unchanged.
EXAMINATION: BP 121/78 mmHg, weight 56 kg, BMI 22.4 (normal). Scalp shows erythematous patches with fine scale; retroauricular mild erythema. No lesions elsewhere.
IMPRESSION: Limited scalp psoriasis flare.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase clobetasol to BD on scalp for 2 weeks, then wean. Continue other topicals and systemic methotrexate. IBS meds unchanged. Return if: rapid spread, pain, fever >38.5°C, or worsening bowel symptoms with blood/mucus.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
clobetasol 0.05% cream – apply BD to scalp lesions – 2 weeks then taper to OD
(calcipotriol, methotrexate, folic acid, mebeverine, ispaghula husk, loperamide unchanged)
